original_value:
Smart Meters are a key component of increasing the power efficiency of the Smart Grid. To help manage the grid effectively, these meters are designed to collect information on power consumption and send it to third parties. With Smart Metering, for the first time, these cloud-connected sensing devices are legally mandated to be installed in the homes of millions of people worldwide. Via a multi-staged empirical study that utilized an open-ended questionnaire, focus groups, and a design probe, we examined how people characterize the tension between the utility of Smart Metering and its impact on privacy. Our findings show that people seek to make abstract Smart Metering data
            accountable
            by connecting it to their everyday practices. Our insight can inform the design of usable privacy configuration tools that help Smart Metering consumers relate abstract data with the real-world implications of its disclosure.

result.paraphrase: Smart Meters play a central role in improving Smart Grid power efficiency. To support effective grid management, they are built to gather power-consumption data and transmit it to third parties. With Smart Metering, these cloud-connected sensing devices are, for the first time, legally required in the homes of millions of people worldwide. Through a multi-stage empirical study using an open-ended questionnaire, focus groups, and a design probe, we investigated how people describe the trade-off between Smart Metering’s usefulness and its privacy impact. Our results indicate that people try to render abstract Smart Metering data accountable by linking it to their everyday practices. This insight can guide the design of usable privacy configuration tools that help Smart Metering consumers connect abstract data to the real-world consequences of disclosing it.
